text:
alex: FYI — noticed a regressed p99 for short-context chat after yesterday's kernel-autotune merge on Ampere pools. It's most visible on the chat-short workload tag.

alex: profile snapshot (staging ampere cluster):
```
model: gptx-7b-8k, workload=chat-short
window: 2026-03-17T22:10-22:40Z
p50  12ms  p95 48ms  p99 186ms  (baseline p99 ~65ms)
hotspots:
  34% kernel_pick::select_best_kernel(arch=ampere)
  21% matmul_longseq_opt::launch (high startup cost)
  14% kv_cache::warmup_handoff
  8% continuous_batcher::schedule
  6% memcpy + cuda memcpy async stalls
```

maria: damn, 3x at p99 for short ctx. Was autotune flip committed to default policy?

alex: yes, merged PR 5892 yesterday that expands kernel candidates and allows the autotuner to promote picks after 15min of 'better' throughput.

cheng: quick hypothesis: autotune picked the long-seq-optimized matmul kernel because it slightly beats others on aggregated windowed throughput (driven by a few long requests), but that kernel has high per-inference startup overhead that dominates for seq <= 64. Combined with continuous batching now being more aggressive, effective micro-batch sizes are small and startup dominates. Also KV warmup gets thrashy on the prefill->decode handoff.

sam: can we confirm by forcing the pre-change kernel for the tag? If that drops p99 back to baseline then autotune is culprit.

alex: ran a quick canary this morning: pinned kernel to smallseq_matmul_v1 for chat-short -> p99 back to 68ms, p95 50ms. So yes.

lee: immediate mitigation options:
- rollback the autotune promotion (revert PR)
- restrict autotune promotions to seq >= 128 or require per-seqlen stratification
- add hysteresis so a pick needs stable win across 3 windows and >=10k samples
- fallback rule: if seq < 64 favor decode-prefill path and smallseq kernels

maria: prefer not to full revert if we can patch heuristics quickly. Can we push a hotfix to the autotuner config to ignore seq < 96 for promotion?

cheng: yes, that should be a small config change. Two follow-ups: ensure autotune stores per-arch+seqlen stats (we currently aggregate across seq buckets) and stop using aggregated throughput metric — use latency-sensitive objective for shortctx.

alex: also observed KV cache warming patterns: when we route a request from prefill->decode with this longseq kernel, KV warmup takes longer and sometimes triggers eviction churn in prefix cache, which then hurts next requests — amplifies p99.

sam: ops ask: do we want an immediate rollback on prod ampere pools while hotfix lands?

ops-bot: prod-rollback suggestion: create a rollback ticket and pin affected pools to previous kernel. I can initiate if owners approve.

maria: do it on a narrow set first (chat-short tag on ampere-1 and ampere-2). We want to reduce blast radius.

deploy-bot: rolling pin start -> ampere-1: pin smallseq_matmul_v1 for workloads matching tag:chat-short (canary: 2 nodes)

cheng: I'll prepare PR to change autotune promotion policy: add seqlen cutoff and require per-seqlen stats + latency objective for shortctx. Drafting now.

lee: test plan:
1) patch config in staging and run repro script (scripts/repro/shortseq_profile.sh) across ampere-staging variants
2) verify p99 returns to baseline and that long-seq workloads unaffected
3) run 6hr canary on prod pinned nodes

alex: repro script output snippet (staging):
```
$ ./scripts/repro/shortseq_profile.sh --model gptx-7b-8k --seq 32 --qps 40 --duration 5m
p50 11ms p95 49ms p99 70ms  (with pinned kernel)
without pin: p99 190ms
flame: kernel_pick -> matmul_longseq_opt -> kv_warmup
```

maria: great. Cheng, add unit tests for the autotuner to verify per-seqlen isolation and hysteresis. Also add a metric in Console: autotune_promotions{arch,seq_bucket} and an alert if promotions spike >5 in 1h.

cheng: will add tests + metrics. Also adding a guard in runtime: if seq < 64 prefer decode path kernels by default (config flag runtime.shortseq_force_decode=true).

sam: note: this surfaced only on Ampere; other archs (turing/gpu-x) have different start-up costs. We should add arch-aware seqlen thresholds.

alex: agreed. For now apply conservative fix on ampere pools and update autotune codepath.

lee: timeline: can we get staging config + PR today? If yes, patch canary tomorrow morning and widen after 6h of stability.

cheng: PR in draft -> https://git.internal/redwood/infra-autotune/pulls/768 (adds seqlen cutoff, hysteresis, per-arch thresholds). pinged reviewers.

maria: thanks. Folks, after this we should run a cross-workload sweep to ensure no regressions (longseq perf, embedding throughput, and KV-heavy prefill flows).

alex: I'll schedule the sweep and report back. :thumbsup:

sam: curious: any change needed to the kernel picker scoring? maybe add a startup_cost penalty term for small seq?

cheng: yes, plan to augment scoring: score = throughput*(1 - alpha*startup_cost/seq_norm) - beta*latency_p99 where seq_norm is clamp(seq,1,256). That should bias picks away from high-startup kernels for small seq.

maria: perfect. Keep thread updated with canary results.

alex: will do. Closing loop when canary completes.
